 BMW X7 Reliability by Year: Complaints and Recalls, 2019-2026
 The 2022 BMW X7 has drawn the fewest complaints and recalls of any model year in NHTSA's records, and brakes lead the complaints on the updated X7 after it.
 Michael Kahn 
 November 11, 2026
 The 2022 BMW X7 has drawn the fewest owner complaints and recalls of any model year since the big SUV went on sale here, and brake problems lead the complaints against the updated X7 that followed it for 2023.
 Table of Contents 
 Complaints and Recalls by Model Year 
 The 2022 Model Year 
 Brakes on the 2023 Through 2025 X7 
 What Hit the Launch Years 
 Crashes, Fires and Injuries 
 Counting Recent Model Years 
 Checking a Used X7 
 Which X7 Year to Buy 
 Frequently Asked Questions 
 A 2025 BMW Alpina XB7, the Alpina-built version of the X7. Photo: Michael Kahn / The Weekly Driver. 
 I pulled every complaint and recall NHTSA holds for the X7 on November 11, 2026. Owners filed 298 complaints against the 2019 through 2025 model years, and BMW ran 31 separate recall campaigns covering those years.
 Key Takeaways 
 2022 drew 20 complaints and two recalls , the lightest record of any X7 model year.
 Brakes lead all complaints , named in 88 of 305, and 77 of those come from 2023 through 2025 cars.
 Three stability-control campaigns and a brake power-assist recall apply to 2023 through 2025 X7s.
 2019 through 2021 complaints center on electrical, engine and powertrain problems , and those years carry nine to 12 recall campaigns each.
 The 2019 and 2020 starter recall ran twice , in August 2024 and again in September 2025.
 NHTSA records nine crashes, six fires, seven injuries and no deaths in X7 complaints.
 Complaints and Recalls by Model Year 
 NHTSA complaints and recall campaigns for the BMW X7, read November 11, 2026. A campaign that covers several model years counts once in each, so the recall column adds up to more than the 33 campaigns on file. The top category is the component owners named most often for that year. 
 Model year Complaints Recall campaigns Top complaint category 
 2019 48 11 Electrical system 
 2020 56 12 Powertrain 
 2021 49 9 Engine 
 2022 20 2 Other or unknown 
 2023 44 8 Service brakes 
 2024 52 7 Service brakes 
 2025 29 4 Service brakes 
 2026 7 2 Mixed, one each 
 Complaints fall by more than half from 2021 to 2022, then climb back to 44 for 2023 and 52 for 2024. With 56 complaints and 12 campaigns, the 2020 model year carries the most of both.
 The 2022 Model Year 
 Twenty complaints against the 2022 X7 is less than half the 2019 through 2025 average of about 43. Its two recalls are shared with other years: a seat campaign, 22V670000, that also covers 2019 through 2021, and a sunroof campaign, 22V267000, that runs from 2019 to 2023.
 Complaints about 2022 cars spread across many components. Their largest group, six, names no specific part, and electrical complaints come next with five.
 Brakes on the 2023 Through 2025 X7 
 A blue brake caliper behind the 23-inch wheel of a 2025 Alpina XB7. Photo: Michael Kahn / The Weekly Driver. 
 Owners of 2024 X7s named the service brakes in 40 complaints, more than any other component on any model year.
 Brake complaints number 25 for 2023 cars and 12 for 2025 cars.
 Electronic stability control comes second on all three years, and the recalls follow the same parts. BMW ran three stability-control campaigns in 2024: 24V104000 and 24V697000 cover 2023 through 2025 cars, and 24V739000 covers 2023 and 2024.
 On July 1, 2026, NHTSA received campaign 26V422000 for the electric power-assist control module in the hydraulic brake system, covering 2023, 2024 and 2025 X7s.
 What Hit the Launch Years 
 Electrical complaints are the largest group on the 2019 X7, at 23. On 2020 cars powertrain complaints lead with 16, and on 2021 cars the engine leads with 12.
 Recalls on those early years cover a wide spread of parts:
 the fuel pump and the side and window airbags on 2019 cars
 lug bolts on 2019 cars
 the automatic transmission, the steering rack and a front control arm on 2020 cars
 headlights on 2020 and 2021 cars
 the rearview camera on 2019 through 2021 cars, in two campaigns
 hydraulic brakes on 2019 through 2021 cars
 BMW has recalled the starter assembly on 2019 and 2020 X7s twice. Campaign 24V576000 arrived in August 2024, and 25V644000 followed in September 2025.
 Crashes, Fires and Injuries 
 Nine X7 complaints report a crash and six report a fire.
 Five complaints list injuries, seven people in all, and none lists a death.
 Counting Recent Model Years 
 A 2019 X7 has had about seven years on the road to collect complaints, and a 2025 X7 about two. Seven complaints and two recalls on the 2026 model cover its first months on sale, and its two campaigns, for windshield and airbag fasteners, apply to 2026 cars only.
 Checking a Used X7 
 NHTSA’s recall lookup at nhtsa.gov/recalls lists open campaigns by VIN, and a BMW dealer can print the service history that shows which were completed.
 On a 2023, 2024 or 2025 car, confirm that 26V422000 and the stability-control campaigns covering that year are closed. On a 2019 or 2020 car, check both starter campaigns, since the second came 13 months after the first.
 Which X7 Year to Buy 
 In NHTSA’s files, the 2022 X7 has the lightest record, with 20 complaints and two recalls shared with neighboring years. A 2023 through 2025 car is the newer design, and its brake and stability-control campaigns are the paperwork to see closed before buying. On a 2019 through 2021 car, the starter and early campaigns matter most.
 Frequently Asked Questions 
 What is the most reliable BMW X7 year? 
 The 2022 X7 has the fewest NHTSA complaints and recalls of any model year, with 20 complaints and two recall campaigns, against an average of about 43 complaints for the 2019 through 2025 model years.
 What BMW X7 years should you avoid? 
 The 2020 X7 carries the most complaints and recalls, at 56 and 12. The 2023 through 2025 cars draw the most brake complaints, so check that their brake and stability-control campaigns are complete before buying one.
 How many recalls does the BMW X7 have? 
 NHTSA lists 33 recall campaigns for the X7: 31 cover the 2019 through 2025 model years, and two apply only to 2026 cars. One campaign often covers several years, so the per-year counts add up to more.
 What are the most common BMW X7 problems? 
 Owners name the service brakes in 88 of the X7’s 305 complaints, the electrical system in 67, and the engine and powertrain in about 40 each. Electronic stability control appears in 41.
 Does the BMW X7 have brake problems? 
 Brakes are the most-named component in X7 complaints, and 77 of the 88 brake complaints involve 2023 through 2025 cars. BMW recalled those years in July 2026 for the brake system’s electric power-assist control module, campaign 26V422000.
 Is a used 2019 BMW X7 a good buy? 
 A 2019 X7 carries 11 recall campaigns, including two for the starter assembly. It can be a sound used buy if every campaign shows as completed on that VIN.
 Has anyone died in a BMW X7 crash reported to NHTSA? 
 X7 complaints filed with NHTSA list nine crashes, six fires and seven injuries, and none reports a death.
 Is the BMW X7 reliable? 
 Its record depends on the year. The 2022 model has the fewest complaints, the 2020 has the most, and the 2023 through 2025 cars concentrate their complaints on the brakes and stability control.
 Does the Alpina XB7 share the X7’s record? 
 The Alpina XB7 is built on the X7 at the same Spartanburg plant. NHTSA’s complaint database has no separate Alpina XB7 entry.
 Where does this data come from? 
 NHTSA’s complaint and recall records for the BMW X7, by model year, which I pulled on November 11, 2026.
 The manufacturer provided the vehicle, a 2025 BMW Alpina XB7, and it supplied the photography published here. No driving evaluation informed this article. 
 Michael Kahn 
 Michael Kahn is the writer, photographer, and publisher behind The Weekly Driver. He cares about how cars drive and what they're like to own. He covers automobile industry news, car shows and events, and new car reviews. The reviews come from behind the wheel: day trips that favor back routes, treating a good meal as half the reason to go. He directs and produces the visual media, matching each car to a setting and mood that fit it. When he's not reviewing new cars, Michael races paddleboards, camels, and ostriches, along with the occasional exotic car on the racetrack, and has driven in every state and country visited.
